title: Thailand: Bangkok flooding triggers disaster declaration
summary: Rainfall over the past three days has caused heavy flooding in the Thai capital. A state of disaster has been declared in all 50 districts in Bangkok.

image.caption: Bangkok's governor said the eastern parts of the city were most impactedImage: Josh Smith/REUTERS

blocks.text: Authorities in Bangkok on Saturday declared a disaster across 50 districts in Thailand's capital after days of heavy rainfall caused severe flooding.
Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said the eastern parts of the city were impacted most.

blocks.caption: Bangkok's governor urges residents to move cars to higher groundImage: AP Video/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

items: Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said the situation posed a threat to life
Emergency ​advisory for ⁠people living near canals to move possessions to ​higher ground
Bangkok city officials open shelter for evacuees

blocks.text: Chadchart said almost 300 millimeters (11.8 inches) of rain had fallen since Thursday afternoon and warned that more rain was expected.

"The rain keeps falling and we are doing our best. We are trying to pump the water out, but the water in canals are full," the governor said on social media and advised residents to move their possessions to higher ground.
"The risk areas are those who live near canals. Every canal is now filled," he said.
Chadchart urged bedridden patients dependent on life-saving medical equipment to consider a temporary stay in hospital.

blocks.caption: Thailand's Meteorological Department warned the heavy rain would persist in most parts of the country through SundayImage: Alex Ogle/AFP

blocks.text: Floods evoke memories of deadly 2011 deluge
"The water keeps coming in. It's hard to go out now. It's like at my waist level now," local vendor Somkid Pheuk-ngam, told the AFP news agency.
"I cannot go anywhere. I have been closing my shop for two days now," she told AFP, adding that while she often gets flooded, "I think this time is worse than the 2011 flood."
Flooding across Thailand in 2011 killed more than 500 people and damaged millions of homes.

Thailand's Meteorological Department warned the heavy rain would persist in most parts of the country through Sunday and pointed to a strong low-pressure system dominating the central region and strengthening monsoon conditions.
